svg.title: Choosing a Power BI Semantic Model Storage Mode
svg.desc: A decision tree. The root question asks what a table needs: a full copy loaded into memory routes to Import; always-current source-of-truth queries route to DirectQuery; and OneLake Delta data with no refresh routes to Direct Lake. Direct Lake then branches again into Direct Lake on OneLake, the default for most models, versus Direct Lake on SQL, needed only for SQL-endpoint security under delegated identity or when DirectQuery fallback is required. A warning node describes a real trap: basing a Direct Lake on SQL table on a SQL view forces every query against it into DirectQuery fallback without changing the model's displayed mode.
svg.text: Choosing a Power BI Storage Mode: Import vs DirectQuery vs Direct Lake
A decision tree — start at freshness need, branch on data location and scale, land on the tradeoff that matches your report
How fresh must the report data be,
and where does the source data live?
Data copied into the model's in-memory
VertiPaq cache — fast, but a snapshot.
required to see new source rows.
Every visual fires a live query against
the source — no copy, always current.
None needed for freshness — but query
latency lands on every report interaction.
Reads Delta tables straight from OneLake —
avoids both import copy and per-query SQL.
refresh — reflects the last successful frame.
Pairs import-mode speed with DirectQuery-like freshness
SUB-DECISION — DIRECT LAKE ON ONELAKE vs DIRECT LAKE ON SQL
OneLake; the endpoint page offers both
faster query performance · no SQL endpoint coupling
This is the mode Desktop and the service create by default
Needed when SQL analytics endpoint security
rules apply under delegated identity, or when
→ CAN fall back to DirectQuery (3 triggers →)
1. Query targets a SQL analytics endpoint view
2. Queried table has SQL-endpoint row-level security
3. The Delta table exceeds a capacity guardrail
Governed by the model's DirectLakeBehavior property
(no effect on Direct Lake on OneLake models)
On fallback: reads the SQL endpoint directly —
escapes framing point-in-time, returns latest data,
typically slower than a resident Direct Lake read
Antipattern: SQL view as a Direct Lake on SQL base table forces every query into fallback
TRADEOFF SCORECARD — WHAT EACH MODE OPTIMIZES FOR
No copy — lazy column load from OneLake
Direct Lake connections fail when this tenant
setting is active — Direct Lake must route
through public endpoints, so it is incompatible
with the strictest network isolation posture.
Queries reflect the last successful frame, not
the live table. Mid-ETL writes stay invisible
until the next frame — disable automatic
updates and frame deliberately during loads.
V-Order and a ~1 GB BinSize target speed
Fabric Atlas — original diagram, July 2026. Not a Microsoft asset; distinct layout/palette from power-bi-consumption.svg and semantic-model-storage-modes.svg.

g.title: What does this table need? — Root question: pick a storage mode per table from freshness need and data location.
Import — Data copied into an in-memory VertiPaq model; needs a refresh schedule to stay current.
DirectQuery — Every query forwards to the source, so results always reflect current data — at a latency cost.
Direct Lake — Reads Delta tables in OneLake directly, on demand, with no import copy and no refresh schedule.
Which Direct Lake flavor? — Sub-decision: Direct Lake on OneLake (default) vs Direct Lake on SQL (security/fallback needs).

g.aria-label: Trap: SQL views force DirectQuery fallback
g.title: Trap: SQL views force DirectQuery fallback — A Direct Lake on SQL table built on a SQL view silently forces every query into DirectQuery fallback.
